German Language Level A1 certificate is recognized by the German Embassy as proof of the basic knowledge of German. This enables you to apply for a visa for the subsequent immigration of your spouse.

At a Glance

  • Flexible timing and from any location

  • Exercises with plenty of variety

Engaging Class Activities at LangNation

  • Interactive Grammar and Vocabulary Exercises:Strengthen your foundation with fun, hands-on activities.

body.curriculum:
Course Contents

Module 1: Basics of German

  • Introduction to the German alphabet and pronunciation
  • Basic greetings and introductions
  • Numbers, days, months, and seasons

Module 4: Communication Skills

  • Asking and answering simple questions
  • Introducing oneself and providing basic information
  • Talking about daily routines and preferences

Module 2: Everyday Vocabulary

  • Common nouns, verbs, and adjectives
  • Essential phrases for shopping, dining, and travel
  • Describing people, places, and objects

Module 5: Listening and Reading Comprehension

  • Understanding simple texts and audio clips
  • Recognizing key information from dialogues
  • Building listening skills for common scenarios

Module 3: Grammar Foundations

  • Articles (definite and indefinite)
  • Personal pronouns and sentence structure
  • Present tense conjugation of regular and irregular verbs

Module 6: Cultural Insights

  • Introduction to German culture and traditions
  • German holidays, festivals, and etiquette basics

Assessment and Certification:

  • Practice exercises and quizzes to track progress
  • Final assessment to receive A1 level certification

This course is ideal for beginners aiming to build a solid foundation in German and communicate confidently in basic everyday situations.

Placement Test/ Einstufungstest

Placement test is not required for A1 level.

Technical requirements for the online course

  • PC, laptop or tablet
  • Headset with microphone
  • Stable internet connection
  • Email address
  • Operating system: Windows, macOS, Android, iOS
  • Browser: Current version of Google Chrome (for all operating systems)

Classroom Procedures & Expectations

PunctualityPreparation
  • Join the class on time. If you are unable to attend, inform your instructor in advance.
  • Come to class with all necessary materials (e.g., notebook, pen, headphones, and any assignments).
Active ParticipationMute when Not Speaking
  • Engage in class activities, discussions, and exercises. Speak up, ask questions, and contribute to group work.
  • Keep your microphone muted when not speaking to minimize background noise.
Camera On (When Possible)Stay Focused
  • Keep your camera on to maintain focus and create a more interactive and engaging environment.
  • Avoid distractions during class (e.g., browsing the internet, using social media). Stay engaged and on task.
Respect and CourtesyEffort and Engagement:
  • Treat your instructor and classmates with kindness and respect at all times. Listen when others are speaking, and allow everyone to share their thoughts.
  • Give your best effort in all tasks, whether it's speaking, writing, or listening. Always strive to improve and help others do the same.
Ask for Help When NeededLanguage Use
  • If you don't understand something, ask questions! Our goal is to support your learning every step of the way.
  • Try to use German as much as possible in the classroom. Don’t worry about making mistakes practice is key to improvement.

Copyright and Plagiarism Policy

All students are expected to respect intellectual property rights by properly citing sources and avoiding plagiarism. Copying or using someone else's work without proper attribution is a violation of academic integrity and will result in appropriate consequences.

body.curriculum:

  • Engaging in debates, expressing feelings and emotions, and offering advice
  • Role-playing scenarios for business, travel, and social interactions

Module 6: Cultural Insights and Practical Use

body.description:
Welcome to LangNation Language Institute

LangNation is your ultimate destination for mastering the German language. Our certified online courses are designed for beginners and advanced learners alike, offering flexible schedules and expert guidance. With a focus on real-world communication and cultural understanding, LangNation equips you with the skills to succeed in academic, professional, and personal settings. Start your journey to fluency in German with us today!

German Language Level A1 -B1 certificate is recognized by the German Embassy as proof of the basic knowledge of German. This enables you to apply for a visa for the subsequent immigration of your spouse.
At a Glance
  • Flexible timing and from any location
  • Individual mentoring from your tutor
  • Exercises with plenty of variety
  • Interesting and up-to-date topics
  • Free online placement test
  • Maximum number of participants: 10

Engaging Class Activities at LangNation

  • Role-Playing and Simulations: Practice real-life conversations in everyday and professional settings.

  • Group Discussions: Build confidence and fluency through collaborative dialogues on diverse topics.

  • Interactive Grammar and Vocabulary Exercises: Strengthen your foundation with fun, hands-on activities.

  • Cultural Workshops: Gain insights into German culture, traditions, and etiquette.
  • Listening and Speaking Drills: Enhance pronunciation and comprehension with practical exercises.
body.curriculum:
Course Contents

Module 1: Foundations (A1 Level)

  • German alphabet, pronunciation & spelling rules
  • Basic greetings, introductions, polite expressions
  • Numbers, dates, time, days, months, seasons
  • Basic sentence structure (Subject–Verb–Object)

Module 2: Vocabulary Building (A1–A2)

  • Common nouns, verbs, adjectives
  • Family, food, travel, work, health
  • Describing people, places, objects
  • Daily-use expressions & phrases

Module 3: Everyday Communication (A1 Level)

  • Asking & answering simple questions (W-questions)
  • Introducing yourself (name, job, nationality)
  • Talking about daily routines (Ich gehe, ich esse…)
  • Basic conversations in shops, restaurants, transport

Module 4: Intermediate Communication (A2 Level)

  • Talking about past (Perfekt tense)
  • Giving opinions & making suggestions
  • Talking about plans & future (werden)
  • Conversations in work, appointments, doctors

Module 5: Grammar Basics (A1 Level)

  • Articles (der, die, das / ein, eine)
  • Personal pronouns (ich, du, er, sie…)
  • Present tense (regular + common irregular verbs)
  • Modal verbs (können, müssen, wollen)
  • Sentence formation & word order

Module 6: Grammar Expansion (A2 Level)

  • Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II)
  • Dative & accusative cases
  • Prepositions (mit, für, bei, von…)
  • Reflexive verbs (sich waschen, sich freuen)
  • Separable verbs (anrufen, einkaufen) 

Module 7: Reading & Listening Skills (A1–A2)

  • Understanding short texts, emails, notices
  • Listening to everyday conversations
  • Extracting key information
  • Building comprehension strategies

Module 8: Advanced Communication (B1 Level)

  • Expressing opinions, arguments, reasons
  • Describing experiences & events
  • Talking about work, education, goals
  • Formal vs informal communication

Module 9: Advanced Grammar (B1 Level)

  • Präteritum (war, hatte, ging…)
  • Konjunktiv II (würde, könnte, hätte…)
  • Passive voice (werden + Partizip II)
  • Relative clauses (der, die, das…)
  • Nebensätze (weil, dass, obwohl, wenn)

Module 10: Speaking & Writing Skills (A2–B1)

  • Writing emails, letters, short texts
  • Speaking in real-life situations
  • Role plays (job interview, doctor, office)
  • Presentation & discussion practice

Module 11: Cultural Insights

  • German culture, traditions, etiquette
  • Work culture in Germany
  • Important holidays & festivals like Oktoberfest and Christmas
  • Social behavior & communication style 

Module 12: Exam Preparation & Real-Life Integration (B1 Level)

  • Complete exam training (Goethe / TELC B1 format)
  • Practice for all sections: Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking
  • Time management strategies for exams
  • Model tests with evaluation and feedback

Assessment & Certification

  • Weekly quizzes & assignments
  • Level-wise mock tests (A1, A2, B1)
  • Speaking evaluations
  • Final exam (B1 Certification Level)

This course is ideal for beginners aiming to build a solid foundation in German and communicate confidently in basic everyday situations.

Materials & Methodology

Course & Work BookNotes of LangNationGerman StoriesMock tests
Live SessionsIndividual tasksExams PreparationQuizzes

Teaching Style:

      • Live interactive sessions
      • Daily practice tasks
      • Speaking-focused learning
      • Real-life scenario training
      • Continuous feedback

Classroom Procedures & Expectations

PunctualityPreparation
  • Join the class on time. If you are unable to attend, inform your instructor in advance.
  • Come to class with all necessary materials (e.g., notebook, pen, headphones, and any assignments).
Active ParticipationMute when Not Speaking
  • Engage in class activities, discussions, and exercises. Speak up, ask questions, and contribute to group work.
  • Keep your microphone muted when not speaking to minimize background noise.
Camera On (When Possible)Stay Focused
  • Keep your camera on to maintain focus and create a more interactive and engaging environment.
  • Avoid distractions during class (e.g., browsing the internet, using social media). Stay engaged and on task.
Respect and CourtesyEffort and Engagement:
  • Treat your instructor and classmates with kindness and respect at all times. Listen when others are speaking, and allow everyone to share their thoughts.
  • Give your best effort in all tasks, whether it's speaking, writing, or listening. Always strive to improve and help others do the same.
Ask for Help When NeededLanguage Use
  • If you don't understand something, ask questions! Our goal is to support your learning every step of the way.
  • Try to use German as much as possible in the classroom. Don’t worry about making mistakes practice is key to improvement.

Copyright and Plagiarism Policy

All students are expected to respect intellectual property rights by properly citing sources and avoiding plagiarism. Copying or using someone else's work without proper attribution is a violation of academic integrity and will result in appropriate consequences.
